A 70 year old aunt asked me to help her buy a conceal carry handgun. (Not her first gun, but she hasn't purchased anything new in a few decades.)

One of her biggest concerns are wild dogs in the public park lands where she walks and hikes. (Guns are legal to carry.)

The challenge is that she has some Arthritis. She has the hand strength to comfortably rack the slide on a .22, but not a 9mm. We tried every 9mm I own and it was just too much for her hands.

A search for handgun+Arthritis pointed to 22's or maybe a revolver.

A 22 is just so under powered self defense, but maybe that would be easiest to fire?

Are there any 9mm's that are known to have an easy slide action?

Should we be looking at a 32 ACP?

Or, maybe we need to focus on finding the right revolver?

Any insights are appreciated.

I personally disagree "A 22 is just so under powered self defense"

If you really believe that you could try .22 magnum or .25 acp. Most slide actions on conventional carry guns(.380, 9, 40, 45) are all going to have tougher slide action naturally.

Also, have your aunt shoot a 9mm before buying one(if you decide on one). If she has trouble with racking the slide she most likely will have trouble with managing recoil.

40gr .22 Magnum vs ballistics gel 36gr .22 LR vs ballistics gel

Sig P238 it's only a .380 but it's the one of the best .380s and it is very easy to rack and shoot well. Plus some models come with hogue rubber grips that further reduce recoil to the point it shoots like a .22

I don't have arthritis, but do have weak grip strength due to muscle issues. When picking out my first handgun I rented a P238 at my local range twice. The gun is super easy to rack and shoot, and It was a serious contender for my first handgun. I ended up training my grip strength a bit and going with a glock 26 that I could rack without too much issue -- now working up to get a glock 27 after I master the 9mm.

You can also get a slide pull charging handle for glocks as well as slide grip tape, kinda goofy looking but you cant knock it if it'll help with racking the slide safely.

The canik tp9sfx also has a side charging handle. I've got a friend that has one and it's kinda cool at first but in practice I'm not a huge fan of making a handgun more bulky. He ended up not using his within the first range trip.
Sounds like a job for a revolver in .38 Special +P, or perhaps a .327 magnum.

I've been in this boat somewhat and I found a couple of things. No.1: revolvers are out of question: there's going to be difficult to cock a single action, and impossible to pull the double action, and No.2: that the shape of the slide makes a world of difference. In particular, on Glocks it is possible to install a rear plate with "wings" sticking out that help racking. Also, a gun with a red dot is easy to rack by grabbing the sight. So, if the budget is not a factor, I would look at Walther PPQ with RMR or Docter first (my wife has a Q5). Failing that, have a look at well broken in Beretta Px4, where she can grab the slide safeties.

P.S. Do not forget the loading of magazines and make sure she uses UpLula.

P.P.S. Another possible option is a .380. You aren't going to find one with an optical sight, but Glock 42 with Tang Down Tactical Racker is very easy to rack. Also a possibility is the newfanged S&W Shield 380 EZ, although I don't have a personal experience with it yet.

I know it's kind of a airshit, but I have a Walther CCP. Due to it being gas delayed blowback it has a lighter recoil spring and is easier to rack. It also has the softest recoil of any small medium handgun I have handled. I say airshit because it's made by Umarex. I have never actually had a problem with it other than the recall to fix the safety.
